They send only the question or the text they are working on, and this computer answers from its own copy of your notes. Uses the model chosen for Ask, write and summarize.

voiceTyping.title: Voice typing
voiceTyping.desc: Speak and your words appear in the note.
limitations: Works best in a quiet place with one person speaking.
Accuracy depends on language and accent. Lite and Standard are most accurate in English; Best covers about 25 languages.
Punctuation and names can be wrong, so check the text before you insert it.

summarizeRecordings.title: Ask, write and summarize
summarizeRecordings.desc: Ask questions about a note and have it make changes you approve. Fix, rewrite or shorten selected text. Summarize notes and recordings, list key points and suggest titles.
summarizeRecordings.bestRouting: Ask and summaries use {{ask}}. Writing tools stay on {{write}}.
limitations: Results can miss or get details wrong, so check them before you rely on them.
Standard is fastest and works best in English. Best handles other languages better, but is slower and needs more memory.
Summaries, titles, key points and questions use the first 8,000 characters of a note.
Writing tools work on up to 3,000 characters of selected text.
Changes are only made after you review and apply them, and can be undone.

describeImages.title: Describe images
describeImages.desc: Get a short description of an image to add as a caption.
limitations: Descriptions are short and in English.
Descriptions can be wrong or miss details, so check them before you use them.
To copy text from an image, use Extract text instead.

transcribeRecordings.title: Transcribe recordings
limitations: Accuracy depends on audio quality, background noise, language and accent.
Speakers aren't labelled, so a conversation comes out as one block of text.
Long recordings take a while, and the app has to stay open until it finishes.
Uses the same model as voice typing.

extractText.title: Extract text
extractText.desc: Copy text from photos, scans and PDFs.
limitations: Standard (EasyOCR) reads Latin-script languages only, such as English, French, German, Spanish, Polish and Vietnamese.
Best (Qwen3.5) also reads other scripts, such as Russian, Arabic, Hindi, Chinese, Japanese and Korean, but it can repeat lines or make up words.
Handwriting, low light, blur and tilted photos reduce accuracy.
Reads up to 20 pages of a PDF. Layout, tables and formatting aren't kept.
Best uses the same model as Describe images, so using both downloads it once.

translateNotes.title: Translate notes
translateNotes.desc: Translate notes to and from English. Each language downloads the first time you use it.
limitations: Translates to and from English. Other pairs go through English, which can lose nuance.
The note's language is detected automatically and can be wrong for short or mixed-language notes. You can change it before translating.
Formatting such as bold, links and lists isn't kept in the translation.
Translates up to 400 paragraphs at a time. Each language needs a 13–44 MB download the first time you use it.

searchByMeaning.title: Search by meaning
searchByMeaning.desc: Find notes by what they're about, not only the words in them. Also shows related notes and possible duplicates.
limitations: Searches the text in your notes. Text in photos, PDFs and recordings isn't included yet.
Locked notes and notes in Recently deleted are never indexed.
On a phone, a large first index waits until the phone is charging.

If you remove it now, those devices keep their notes but can no longer sync "{{name}}" with each other. To avoid this, open "{{name}}" on another device and try again.
